data.reasoning: The package is a standard VCS icon theme that clones from its declared upstream GitHub repository (https://github.com/erikdubois/surfn-numixs.git). The PKGBUILD contains only normal variable assignments and standard functions (pkgver, package). The package() function performs reasonable cleanup (removing build scripts and cache files) before installing icons. No suspicious network operations, obfuscated code, or injection patterns are present. The 'inconclusive' verdict from qwen was caused by an API error (HTTP 400) when auditing .gitignore, not by any security concern. Since .gitignore contains no executable code, this tool error should not affect the overall safety verdict.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was triggered by qwen's API failure when auditing .gitignore, which resulted in an 'inconclusive' status for that file. This is a tool error, not a security finding. The deepseek model correctly audited all files including .gitignore and found no issues. The openrouter/free report (advisory: true) also found the package safe but doesn't count as a vote per the rules.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), but this file contains no executable code and poses no security risk
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) on non-executable files like .gitignore should not force an 'inconclusive' package verdict when the file type cannot contain malicious code
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file could not be analyzed due to tool error' and 'file contains suspicious content' when determining overall package safety

For VCS packages with standard patterns (git source, SKIP checksums, simple install functions), models should explicitly confirm the source URL matches the declared upstream to rule out source substitution attacks
